Customize Last Millennium Reanalysis Parameters




The Last Millennium Reanalysis (LMR) uses offline data assimilation with the PAGES 2k proxy database to reconstruct surface temperature over the past 2000 years. This reconstruction employs the Climate Field Reconstruction (CFR) framework to combine proxy observations with climate model simulations. Select your proxy data using the map and filters below, then customize reconstruction parameters. Your reconstruction will run in a GitHub Actions workflow, and results will be stored in your GitHub repository. For more information about the CFR method, visit: https://fzhu2e.github.io/cfr/



Start from a previous reconstruction (optional)

Paste a GitHub URL (blob or raw) to a configs.yml from a previous run, or upload one. Validated and applied to the form below.

? Each seed produces an independent assimilation realization using a different randomly chosen 100-member ensemble and 75% of available proxy records. This Monte Carlo sampling over subsets of prior states and proxy records incorporates uncertainties in covariance estimates and proxy error estimates. Averaging over realizations reduces random errors from individual proxy records with underestimated observation errors. The final reconstruction is the mean over all ensemble members and all realizations (e.g., 10 seeds × 100 members = 1,000-member grand ensemble).




? Distance threshold for spatial correlation in data assimilation. Larger values allow more distant proxies to influence reconstruction.



Check "Show advanced options" to see all parameter choices



? Proportion of available proxies to use in each Monte Carlo iteration (0.75 = 75%)



? Number of ensemble members for the prior. Larger values improve reconstruction quality but increase computation time.
